sources.support: Executor implementations may run a task in the caller, a pooled thread or a new thread; submission does not itself require asynchronous handoff.
Supplied-executor stage placement, inline non-async continuations, exceptional-completion cancellation and lack of interrupt control in the base implementation.
Default sendAsync returns cancelable futures whose cancel(true) attempts exchange cancellation; timing, remote execution and resource release are not immediate guarantees.
Demand is a number of items per subscription, and cancellation eventually stops delivery; it does not directly bound retained bytes or separately submitted tasks.
Final scoped-binding API in Java25, binding/dynamic scope and bounded sharing contract.
Preview status, owner-thread restrictions, cancellation/join/close semantics and scope-based scoped-value binding inheritance.
Permit-based acquisition, fairness at internal ordering points and untimed tryAcquire barging qualification.

casePreparation.classification: Reproducible development cases, not actor executions or unseen holdouts.
casePreparation.separation: Give the actor only sharedActorFixtures, the selected actorFixtures and actorTask. Keep evaluatorExpectations, failureConditions and constraintFlip private. The coordinator can materialize the named files in an isolated directory.
casePreparation.actorTask: Review the supplied metadata bridge for its selected runtime wiring. Return the dominant concurrency decision, whether the current bridge can be retained under the supplied contract, and the owning specialist or smallest change needed. Inspect the actual provider and resource contract; do not implement every concurrency abstraction or upgrade the JDK.

sharedActorFixtures.contract.md: The project compiles and runs on Java21 without preview. A plugin must return CompletionStage<String>. Inline execution and already-completed stages are permitted. Session.readLabel accesses a cached, bounded local value with no blocking I/O; it must run on the exact Java thread that created the Session. The caller has finished its mutations before invoking Bridge.read and holds no lock. No deferred callback is required. A single application owner manages and closes AppExecutors at shutdown; do not close it per request. Performance evidence does not justify adding concurrency here.
sharedActorFixtures.caller.txt: The request thread creates Session, selects the executor named in wiring.txt from the application's AppExecutors, and invokes Bridge.read(session, selectedExecutor). The consumer accepts the returned stage.

casePreparation.fixturePrerequisites: Source fixtures use Java21 APIs and can be inspected without execution. No external dependency or preview feature is required. A coordinator choosing to compile them should use the project's Java21 release target and report its actual runtime separately. They intentionally omit an application main and are not claimed as an executed test harness.

evaluatorExpectations: Trace workerExecutor to the managed worker pool and identify that Session.readLabel would execute on a different Java thread.
